answer: Memory-hard proof of work charges computation per claim. Seed a fresh puzzle with the epoch, account and words harbor, plume and shale; verify its solution and consume the nonce once. N accounts require N separately solved puzzles, so renaming a fixed computing budget cannot increase expected claim throughput. The attacker spends machine time and energy. This assumes no shortcut or reusable solution; set difficulty against expected reward, since cheap hardware can otherwise make farming profitable.
